editorial:
Imagine having all the money in the world but feeling like something is missing. That is exactly where you find Guy Taylor, a rich businessman who seems to have it all. Things get messy when he meets Rachel Bell, a stunning woman who is already married to a sculptor who is barely making ends meet. You get to watch a tense game of attraction and guilt as Guy starts to wonder if his wealth can actually buy the kind of happiness and passion he sees in Rachel's life. It feels like a classic soap opera with a lot of heart and some heavy questions about love and status.

You will really appreciate the acting here, as the tension between the three leads feels very real and awkward. The pacing is steady, though it feels more like a stage play than a big Hollywood movie, which makes the dialogue stand out more. If you enjoy character studies about rich people having mid-life crises, you will love this. Since it is an older TV play, your best bet is to track down a high-quality digital restore. If you can find it for rent on Apple TV or as a physical 4K Blu-ray for your collection, it is definitely worth the upgrade for the crisp picture.
endingExplained: By the end, Guy has to face the truth that his money cannot fix his empty life. After the tension peaks between him, Rachel, and her husband, he realizes that chasing Rachel was more about wanting her passion than the woman herself. He decides to step back and stop interfering in their marriage. He ends up alone but with a better understanding of what he actually wants from his future, leaving the cycle of greed behind.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school dramas and stories about complicated relationships.
